page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the legacy N1 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon processor cores running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% category, with scores of 1107.78 and 2904.55 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 161.64 GB/sec for cached small blocks and approximately 25.29 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, both ranking in the bottom 25%. Computational tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression register in the bottom 10%, while static web serving throughput is limited to 2.46 GB/sec.

Given its legacy hardware profile and lower relative benchmark scores, the n1-standard-4 is positioned as a cost-effective option for workloads that do not demand high-performance computing. It is suitable for basic general-purpose tasks, lightweight web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, and simple background processing queues where resource density is prioritized over raw execution speed.

Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.3 GHz, this instance features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. In benchmark testing, the n1-standard-4 consistently performs in the lower tiers, with stress-ng CPU and memory bandwidth results falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded compression tasks ranking in the bottom 10%.
